scope: Corollary 8.4 (Precision under the uniform spherical prior) of the manuscript “Localization costs and information growth for exact Gaussian observations” (preprints/Localization-costs-and-information-growth-for-exact-Gaussian-observations-September-27-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 140 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 4f43e1443f9fd513), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 51. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let M(d) = o(d2) and 0 < ϵ(d) ≤ 1/10. For learners in the finite-state model of Section 2, uniform-sphere average angular success at least 2/3 requires T(d) ≥ c d log 1 ϵ(d) for an absolute c > 0 and all sufficiently large d. The dimension threshold may depend on the memory sequence.
